items.notes: Spelling checked against the A2 master coursebook and then TDK: the list has "İlahi" unaccented, glossed "chant". Circumflexes would be wrong here, and not merely unnecessary. TDK lists every sense as one Arabic word (ilāhī) and spells both the adjective and the noun plain "ilahi"; only the vocative "Ey Allah'ım" takes İlahî. The senses differ in sound, not spelling: the adjective "divine" is ila:hi: with a LONG final i, this noun is ila:hi with a SHORT one, and the interjection is i'la:hi, stressed on the first syllable. So an î on this card would assert length the hymn does not have. In all senses the l is palatalised ("l ince okunur"). Corrects an earlier note of mine that called ilâhî a different word — it is the same word, and that is not TDK's spelling of it. TDK lists three homographs with three pronunciations: the adjective 'divine' is ila:hi: (both vowels long), the exclamation is i'la:hi (initial stress), and this noun — the hymn — is ila:hi, so the long a is followed by a SHORT final i. The 'l ince okunur' note makes the l clear despite the back vowel. en.wiktionary's /iˈlaː.hiː/ transcribes the adjective, not this entry.
